text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT triggered: latency_slo_breach on canary-cluster-encoders (p99 > 2s)

metrics-bot: Canary encoder pool p95 jumped from 420ms -> 1.6s in the last 3m. p99 ~ 3.4s. error-rate stable. streaming stall rate increased by ~8%.

alicia (oncall): seeing it too. alert came in at 09:22 UTC. Canary rollout of encoder-service:v1.3 started ~09:15 UTC.

mike (sre): confirmed across the canary region (eu-west). tail latency spike aligned w/ encoder v1.3 deploys to 10% traffic.

sam (runtime): suspected change: quantization tweak + new fused-attention kernel in v1.3. It changed KV cache layout slightly. Might be causing extra GPU memory copies and stalls.

jen (prod-eng): cc @sam @mike — this is on our canary. How fast can we shift traffic back to v1.2? We should avoid full rollback until we confirm root cause.

alicia (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce canary traffic to 0% 2) scale up encoder pool by +2 nodes for graceful draining 3) divert new requests to dedicated pool. Starting now.

carlos (infra): scaling up +2 node request accepted, ETA ~90s.

metrics-bot: Traffic shift executed: canary traffic -> 0% at 09:26:12 UTC. p95 dropped to 480ms within 40s, p99 down to 700ms but streaming stalls still at +4% vs baseline.

customer-success: Flagging two affected customers — alpha-app and billing-pro — reported slow responses and some streaming timeouts during the window. No data loss. CS is pinging them with a brief update.

mike (sre): streaming stalls linger. logs show repeated "KVCacheLock contended" messages for encoder shards on worker-7. stack traces show stalled write path during flush.

sam (runtime): that aligns with the quantization change — new path serializes cache updates differently. Might hold locks longer under specific token patterns (long prefix). Reproducer in local later today.

alicia (oncall): is this a correctness regression or performance-only? Any risk if we keep v1.3 in canary at 0%?

jen (prod-eng): correctness seems fine. No user-visible content regressions reported. This is performance/timing only. Keeping at 0% is safe for now.

deploy-bot: Rollout action: set traffic for encoder-service:v1.3 -> 0%. Command: `./deployctl shift encoder-service --from v1.3 --to v1.2 --percent 100`

alicia (oncall): executed the deployctl command at 09:26:12 UTC (confirmed).

metrics-bot: p99 back to baseline (~650ms) at 09:27:05 UTC. streaming stall rate improved to +1%. Still seeing rare stalls on worker-7.

mike (sre): isolating worker-7. Logs show intermittent IO bursts to /scratch during heavy batching. Could be NVMe GC coinciding with certain token lengths.

carlos (infra): checking node health and disk io metrics. NVMe gc cycles flagged on worker-7 shortly before spike. Will repro and attach OS metrics.

sam (runtime): two-fold hypothesis: (1) quantization path in v1.3 amplifies stall when storage IO bursts occur, (2) fused-attention kernel increases memory pressure causing more GC. Need root-cause repro with load gen.

jen (prod-eng): next steps: 1) keep v1.3 at 0% canary, 2) add NVMe monitoring alert for GC, 3) schedule rollback+probe test if we see re-introduction.

customer-success: update sent to customers at 09:40 UTC: "We observed elevated request latencies during a canary encoder rollout. We reduced canary traffic and latencies returned to normal. Investigating root cause; will follow up."

alicia (oncall): I'm going to create a short incident doc and handoff to daytime oncall in 30m. @mike can you take the lead on post-mortem? @sam to own repro.

mike (sre): taking lead on the post-mortem. I'll pull the relevant trace spans and correlate with NVMe metrics.

sam (runtime): will run reproduction with quantized model + synthetic long-prefix load, and test on worker-7 replica. Expect results in 2-3h.

carlos (infra): I'll reimage worker-7 and run fio to stress NVMe; will attach iostat and nvme logs.

alicia (oncall): mitigation summary pinned: traffic -> 0%, +2 nodes for capacity, isolated worker-7 for deeper debug. No further customer impact after traffic shift.

metrics-bot: summary snapshot at 09:35 UTC: canary p95 480ms (baseline 420ms), p99 650ms (baseline 430ms), streaming stall rate +1% (baseline 0.2%).

jen (prod-eng): follow-ups: - schedule canary rollback if repro shows it's solely v1.3 - add circuit-breaker to abort future rollouts if p99 > 1.5s for >1m - add telemetry counters for KV cache lock hold-time.

alicia (oncall): handing off with notes to next oncall at 10:00 UTC. Incident severity: Sev2 (partial SLO impact, limited customer reports).

incident-bot: Handoff: alicia (oncall) -> tay (oncall-next) at 10:00 UTC. Link to incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incident/2150003141

tay (oncall-next): acknowledged. I'll pick up status in the morning and ping for any rollbacks if needed.

mike (sre): added immediate action items in the runbook: collect full flamegraphs for encoder v1.2 vs v1.3 under identical load, gather NVMe GC traces, check batching heuristics.

sam (runtime): noted. I'll attempt a micro-patch to shorten KV cache lock windows; if that repros improvement, we'll consider a v1.3.1 patch before re-rollout.

alicia (oncall): thanks everyone. Closing realtime response. Will update incident thread once post-mortem draft is ready. :white_check_mark:
